# Model and source

* Citation: Fan HH, McCune JS, Kanakry CG, Mager DE. Hybrid Systems Modeling of
  Donor T-Cell Responses and Graft-Versus-Host-Disease After Posttransplantation
  Cyclophosphamide Administration. CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol.
  2026;15(4):e70252. doi:10.1002/psp4.70252.
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70252>
* PK layer: Campagne O, et al. J Pharm Pharm Sci. 2019;22(1):612-629
  (doi:10.18433/jpps30608), packaged separately as
  `Campagne_2019_cyclophosphamide_mouse`.

Posttransplantation cyclophosphamide (PTCy) prevents graft-versus-host disease
(GVHD) after HLA-haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT). Fan 2026
built a hybrid systems model of a murine MHC-haploidentical HCT
(B6C3F1 -> B6D2F1) in which recipients received vehicle or PTCy 5, 10, 25, 50
or 100 mg/kg/day intraperitoneally on days 3 and 4. The packaged model is the
mechanistic part of that hybrid:

1. **PK** of cyclophosphamide (CY), 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide (4HCY) and
   carboxyethylphosphoramide mustard (CEPM): the Campagne 2019 mouse model
   (central, peripheral and brain extracellular-fluid compartments for each
   compound), run with its typical values (Methods S1, Table S2). Doses are
   in umol/kg; outputs `Cc`, `Cc_4ohctx`, `Cc_cepm` are in umol/L.
2. **Drug effect**: a sigmoid Emax function of central 4HCY feeds four
   signal-transduction transit compartments; the last one (`transit4`, M4 in
   the paper, 1/day) is a first-order removal rate applied to every T cell
   (Eqs. 2-4).
3. **Donor T-cell kinetics** of cytotoxic CD8+ (`tc_`), helper CD4+Foxp3-
   (`th_`) and regulatory CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ (`treg_`) cells recirculating between
   blood and spleen, lymph node, liver, intestine and lung (the Ganusov-Tomura
   recirculation model), with density-dependent proliferation, death in blood,
   a delayed sigmoid thymic output and saturable homing capacity in spleen,
   lymph node and liver (Eqs. 5-11). Spleen, lymph node and intestine
   residence is gamma-distributed through two sub-compartments.

The outputs are the measured quantities: blood concentrations in cells/uL
(`tc_blood_conc`, `th_blood_conc`, `treg_blood_conc`; Eq. 12 divides the blood
amount by the blood volume 77 uL/g x body weight) and the amounts in spleen
(`spleen_*`), lymph node (`lnode_*`) and liver (`*_liver`) in cells.

The paper's third layer, a scikit-learn neural network mapping the simulated
exposure and T-cell amounts to the GVHD clinical score, is **not** included:
its trained weights were not published (see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Fan_2026_cyclophosphamide_mouse_qsp")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

The model was calibrated on the Wachsmuth 2019 preclinical data set: lethally
irradiated B6D2F1 recipients given 10 x 10^6 T-cell-depleted bone marrow cells
and 40 x 10^6 splenocytes from B6C3F1 donors on day 0, then vehicle or PTCy on
days 3 and 4 (Figure 1). Donor T-cell subsets were counted by flow cytometry in
blood, peripheral lymph nodes, spleen and liver on days 7, 21 and 200; each
mouse contributed one time point, so the parameters were estimated by a
naive-pooled fit with a proportional residual error. Cyclophosphamide and
metabolite concentrations were not measured. The model has no between-animal
variability, so every simulation below is a single typical mouse per arm.

# Body weight (replicates Figure S2)

Body weight enters only through the blood volume. The paper describes each dose
cohort's measured weight course with a piecewise polynomial in days after
transplant (Methods S2). The function below transcribes the authors' code
(the coefficients are those of Data S2 at full precision); it returns grams.

```{r body-weight}
poly_eval <- function(x, coef) {
  # coef = c(a_n, ..., a_1, a_0), highest power first as in the authors' code
  n <- length(coef) - 1
  out <- 0
  for (k in seq_along(coef)) out <- out + coef[k] * x^(n - k + 1)
  out
}
# Each segment: polynomial coefficients (highest power first) whose constant
# term is fixed so the curve passes through the anchor weight at the segment's
# left boundary, exactly as in the authors' code.
seg_anchor <- function(x, anchor_t, anchor_w, coef_no_const) {
  const <- anchor_w - poly_eval(anchor_t, c(coef_no_const, 0))
  poly_eval(x, c(coef_no_const, const))
}
bw_mouse <- function(t, dose) {
  if (dose == 0) {
    return(poly_eval(t, c(0.00011362506735482164, -0.00826056901856251, 0.19185179148275394, -1.6063315340649584, 19.117606066318015)))
  }
  if (dose == 5) {
    return(dplyr::case_when(
      t <= 15 ~ poly_eval(t, c(0.061125979247648336, -1.1027353126822668, 19.67747326742453)),
      t <= 40 ~ seg_anchor(t, 15, 16.889788907911406, c(0.01624986014465811, -0.9693092542109911)),
      t <= 80 ~ seg_anchor(t, 40, 15.000615251541532, c(0.004868793656665482, -0.5727178165930265)),
      TRUE ~ seg_anchor(t, 80, 15.462112139814788, c(5.969032333630331e-5, -0.016889608040012938, 1.3088495493688046))
    ))
  }
  if (dose == 10) {
    return(dplyr::case_when(
      t <= 15 ~ poly_eval(t, c(0.07336, -1.1759, 18.9032)),
      t <= 48 ~ seg_anchor(t, 15, 17.7716, c(0.0048, -0.3348)),
      t <= 72 ~ seg_anchor(t, 48, 16.76, c(0, 0.0042, -0.479)),
      TRUE ~ seg_anchor(t, 72, 17.41, c(-1.486e-6, 0.00059, -0.0447))
    ))
  }
  if (dose == 25) {
    return(dplyr::case_when(
      t <= 15 ~ poly_eval(t, c(0.06853947299288776, -0.9254518309015851, 18.184305097213898)),
      t <= 50 ~ seg_anchor(t, 15, 19.723909057089866, c(0.004463157875784329, -0.3054190192384727)),
      t <= 85 ~ seg_anchor(t, 50, 19.18792755115267, c(0.007225692711694881, -0.9698172953804558)),
      TRUE ~ seg_anchor(t, 85, 19.385720275595027, c(-3.7676703012067405e-6, 0.001796149396493317, -0.2516649870739913))
    ))
  }
  if (dose == 50) {
    return(dplyr::case_when(
      t <= 15 ~ poly_eval(t, c(0.0514, -0.7894, 18.4162)),
      t <= 48 ~ seg_anchor(t, 15, 18.1294, c(0.0055, -0.3613)),
      t <= 90 ~ seg_anchor(t, 48, 17.57, c(1.1744e-5, -0.002858, 0.2551, -9.9656)),
      t <= 117 ~ seg_anchor(t, 90, 17.92, c(4.531e-5, -0.019098, 3.0106, -210.3305)),
      TRUE ~ seg_anchor(t, 117, 17.95, c(3.3992e-7, -0.0002232, 0.05455, -5.8599))
    ))
  }
  if (dose == 100) {
    return(dplyr::case_when(
      t <= 20 ~ poly_eval(t, c(0.02865474565453785, -0.5616023455819161, 18.895127739361776)),
      t <= 50 ~ seg_anchor(t, 20, 19.12497908953859, c(0.0033794229763421946, -0.17974428539962584)),
      t <= 130 ~ seg_anchor(t, 50, 20.829438777868425, c(2.3299255973114522e-5, -0.005164356482746972, 0.2240792152083612)),
      TRUE ~ seg_anchor(t, 130, 12.665101019274214, c(-8.111948823347032e-5, 0.04119905641085836, -6.779076502276648))
    ))
  }
  stop("dose must be one of 0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 mg/kg/day")
}

bw_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100), time = seq(0, 200, by = 0.5)) |>
  filter(!(dose == 0 & time > 35), !(dose == 5 & time > 100)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(weight_g = bw_mouse(time, dose)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(bw_grid, aes(time, weight_g)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose, "mg/kg/day"), ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time after transplant (day)", y = "Body weight (g)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S2 of Fan 2026 (spline curves only).")
```

# Dosing input: nominal and as fitted

Equation 1 of the paper describes each PTCy dose as a 9-min zero-order input
starting at day 3 and day 4. In the authors' code the input rate is switched on
when a point of the 0.025-day solution grid falls inside the 9-min window, and
that rate is then applied over the whole preceding 0.025-day step. The dose that
reached the model was therefore 4 times the nominal dose, delivered over
2.975-3.000 and 3.975-4.000 days, at the nominal infusion rate. Figure S1
shows exactly this: the CY peak after 100 mg/kg is about 560 umol/L and the
4HCY peak about 190 umol/L, which a 9-min infusion of 100 mg/kg cannot produce
(it gives a 4HCY peak of about 30 umol/L). The drug-effect parameters (Emax,
EC50, gamma, tau) were calibrated to the day-7 T-cell counts under that input.

The packaged model carries the paper's equations and Table 1 values unchanged.
To reproduce the published figures, this vignette gives the "as fitted" input;
the nominal 9-min input is shown afterwards for contrast. With the nominal input
the calibrated effect of PTCy on day-7 T cells almost disappears.

```{r dosing-helpers}
mw_cy <- 0.261086 # mg/umol, authors' code (Eq. 1 prints 0.261)

ptcy_doses <- function(dose_mgkg, input = c("as_fitted", "nominal")) {
  input <- match.arg(input)
  if (dose_mgkg == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  amt <- dose_mgkg / mw_cy
  if (input == "as_fitted") {
    data.frame(time = c(2.975, 3.975), amt = 4 * amt, dur = 0.025)
  } else {
    data.frame(time = c(3, 4), amt = amt, dur = 9 / 60 / 24)
  }
}

build_events <- function(dose_mgkg, obs_times, input = "as_fitted") {
  dd <- ptcy_doses(dose_mgkg, input)
  obs <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = NA_real_,
                    cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  if (!is.null(dd)) {
    dos <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = dd$time, evid = 1L, amt = dd$amt, dur = dd$dur,
                      cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
    obs <- rbind(dos, obs)
  }
  obs <- obs[order(obs$time, -obs$evid), ]
  # Body weight in kg, time-varying, from the dose cohort's spline
  obs$WT <- bw_mouse(obs$time, dose_mgkg) / 1000
  obs
}

solve_arm <- function(dose_mgkg, obs_times, input = "as_fitted") {
  ev <- build_events(dose_mgkg, obs_times, input)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame",
                         atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6)
  out$dose <- dose_mgkg
  out$input <- input
  out
}
```

# Simulated plasma PK (replicates Figure S1)

```{r pk-sim}
pk_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(2.5, 5, by = 0.0025), 3, 4)))
pk <- bind_rows(lapply(c(5, 25, 100), solve_arm, obs_times = pk_times))

pk_long <- pk |>
  select(time, dose, CY = Cc, `4HCY` = Cc_4ohctx, CEPM = Cc_cepm) |>
  pivot_longer(c(CY, `4HCY`, CEPM), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, c("CY", "4HCY", "CEPM")))

ggplot(mutate(pk_long, conc = ifelse(conc < 1e-6, NA_real_, conc)), aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-6, 1e4)) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte) +
  labs(x = "Time after transplant (day)", y = "Plasma concentration (umol/L)",
       colour = "PTCy (mg/kg/day)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S1 of Fan 2026 (as-fitted dosing input).")

pk_peaks <- pk |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(CY = max(Cc), `4HCY` = max(Cc_4ohctx), CEPM = max(Cc_cepm), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pk_peaks, digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated peak plasma concentrations (umol/L), as-fitted input.")
```

The authors' code gives peaks of 28.1, 140 and 562 umol/L for CY and 9.52,
47.6 and 190 umol/L for 4HCY after 5, 25 and 100 mg/kg (values obtained by the
maintainers by running the deposited code).

```{r pk-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(pk_peaks$CY[pk_peaks$dose == 100] / 562 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(pk_peaks$`4HCY`[pk_peaks$dose == 100] / 190 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(pk_peaks$`4HCY`[pk_peaks$dose == 5] / 9.52 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

# Donor T-cell kinetics (replicates Figure 3)

```{r tcell-sim}
t_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 23, by = 0.05), 7, 21)))
arms <- c(0, 5, 25, 100)
tsim <- bind_rows(lapply(arms, solve_arm, obs_times = t_times))

panel_map <- tibble::tribble(
  ~column, ~subset, ~tissue,
  "tc_blood_conc", "Tc", "Blood (cells/uL)",
  "th_blood_conc", "Th", "Blood (cells/uL)",
  "treg_blood_conc", "Treg", "Blood (cells/uL)",
  "spleen_tc", "Tc", "Spleen (cells)",
  "spleen_th", "Th", "Spleen (cells)",
  "spleen_treg", "Treg", "Spleen (cells)",
  "lnode_tc", "Tc", "Lymph node (cells)",
  "lnode_th", "Th", "Lymph node (cells)",
  "lnode_treg", "Treg", "Lymph node (cells)",
  "tc_liver", "Tc", "Liver (cells)",
  "th_liver", "Th", "Liver (cells)",
  "treg_liver", "Treg", "Liver (cells)"
)

tlong <- tsim |>
  select(time, dose, all_of(panel_map$column)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(panel_map$column), names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |>
  left_join(panel_map, by = "column") |>
  mutate(tissue = factor(tissue, unique(panel_map$tissue)))
```

```{r fig3, fig.height = 9}
# The infused cells leave blood for the tissues within hours of day 0; the
# plot starts at day 0.1, as the paper's figure effectively does.
ggplot(filter(tlong, time >= 0.1), aes(time, value, colour = factor(dose), linetype = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_grid(tissue ~ subset, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after transplant (day)", y = "Donor T cells",
       colour = "PTCy (mg/kg/day)", linetype = "PTCy (mg/kg/day)",
       caption = "Replicates the model curves of Figure 3 of Fan 2026 (as-fitted dosing input; from day 0.1).")
```

The curves reproduce Figure 3: a dose-dependent nadir around day 6-7 that
reaches about 0.1 cells/uL for blood Tc after 100 mg/kg, and convergence of all
arms towards the vehicle curve by day 21 as thymic output starts.

```{r compare-reference}
check_times <- function(dose) if (dose == 0) c(7, 21) else c(7, 21, 200)
cmp_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100), function(d) {
  solve_arm(d, obs_times = check_times(d))
}))
cmp <- cmp_sim |>
  select(dose, time, all_of(ref_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(ref_cols), names_to = "column", values_to = "packaged") |>
  inner_join(ref, by = c("dose", "time", "column")) |>
  mutate(ratio = packaged / reference)

cmp_summary <- cmp |>
  mutate(group = case_when(
    dose == 0 ~ "vehicle, days 7 and 21",
    time == 200 ~ "PTCy, day 200",
    time == 21 ~ "PTCy, day 21",
    dose <= 10 ~ "PTCy 5-10 mg/kg, day 7",
    TRUE ~ "PTCy 25-100 mg/kg, day 7"
  )) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), min_ratio = min(ratio), median_ratio = median(ratio),
            max_ratio = max(ratio), .groups = "drop")
cmp_summary |>
  dplyr::rename("Comparison" = group, "Outputs" = n, "Min ratio" = min_ratio,
                "Median ratio" = median_ratio, "Max ratio" = max_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
               caption = "Packaged model / authors' code, by group (12 outputs per arm and day).")

cmp |>
  filter(time == 7, dose >= 25) |>
  select(dose, column, reference, packaged, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename("PTCy (mg/kg/day)" = dose, "Output" = column, "Authors' code" = reference,
                "Packaged model" = packaged, "Ratio" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Day 7 after PTCy 25-100 mg/kg.")
```

The vehicle arm and day 200 agree to better than 1%, which confirms the
structure, the parameter values, the initial conditions and the body-weight
handling. Day-7 values after 5-10 mg/kg agree within 2% and day-21 values
within about 6%. After 25-100 mg/kg the day-7 values differ by 0.6- to 2.7-fold
(25 mg/kg about 1.4-fold, 50 mg/kg 2.2- to 2.7-fold, 100 mg/kg about 0.6-fold;
the deepest nadirs make these the most sensitive values): the authors' code solves the T-cell
model in 0.025-day steps with the 4HCY concentration held at its end-of-step
value, so during the step that ends at the infusion stop the drug effect runs at
the peak concentration for the whole step. The packaged model couples the PK
and the T-cell layers continuously.

```{r compare-check}
stopifnot(
  all(abs(cmp$ratio[cmp$dose == 0] - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(cmp$ratio[cmp$time == 200] - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(cmp$ratio[cmp$time == 21] - 1) < 0.10),
  all(abs(cmp$ratio[cmp$time == 7 & cmp$dose %in% c(5, 10)] - 1) < 0.02),
  # The two couplings differ most where the depletion is deepest; the bound is
  # the measured spread (0.60-2.66), not a tuning target.
  all(abs(log(cmp$ratio[cmp$time == 7])) < log(3))
)
```

## Nominal 9-min input

```{r nominal-input}
nominal <- bind_rows(lapply(c(25, 100), function(d) {
  bind_rows(solve_arm(d, obs_times = 7, input = "as_fitted"),
            solve_arm(d, obs_times = 7, input = "nominal"))
})) |>
  select(dose, input, tc_blood_conc, th_blood_conc, treg_blood_conc, spleen_tc, tc_liver) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(dose, input), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = input, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(fold = nominal / as_fitted)

nominal |>
  dplyr::rename("PTCy (mg/kg/day)" = dose, "Output" = output, "As fitted" = as_fitted,
                "Nominal 9-min input" = nominal, "Nominal / as fitted" = fold) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Day-7 T cells under the two dosing inputs.")
```

With the nominal input the 100 mg/kg arm loses most of its day-7 depletion
(about 140-fold more T cells in every tissue than with the as-fitted input; the 25 mg/kg arm has about 1.7-fold more), because the 4HCY peak
is about 30 instead of 190 umol/L and stays below the calibrated EC50 of
85 umol/L. Users who simulate other PTCy doses or schedules should know that
the calibrated drug-effect parameters belong to the as-fitted input.

# PKNCA check of the PK layer

The terminal half-life of CY after a single nominal 100 mg/kg input is computed
with PKNCA and compared with the value the paper quotes for CY in mice
(0.19 +/- 0.01 h; Table S1, assumption iv, citing Ramirez 2019). The PK layer
is linear, so the half-life does not depend on the input.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(3, 3.5, by = 1 / 24 / 60 * 2))))
nca_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(c(25, 100), function(d) {
  ev <- build_events(d, obs_times = nca_times, input = "nominal")
  ev <- ev[!(ev$evid == 1 & ev$time > 3.5), ]
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame",
                         atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6)
  out$treatment <- paste0(d, " mg/kg")
  out$id <- 1L
  out
}))

conc_df <- nca_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time_h = (time - 3) * 24) |>
  select(id, treatment, time_h, Cc)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = c("25 mg/kg", "100 mg/kg"), time_h = 0,
                      amt = c(25, 100) / mw_cy)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time_h | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time_h | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Treatment" = treatment, "Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
                "AUC0-inf (umol*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "PKNCA of plasma CY after one nominal 9-min input.")
```

```{r pknca-compare}
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(treatment == "100 mg/kg", PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  transmute(PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_nca,
  reference = data.frame(half.life = 0.19),
  units = c(half.life = "h")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "CY terminal half-life: packaged model vs the value quoted by Fan 2026.")
```

The simulated terminal half-life (0.26 h) is 34% longer than the 0.19 h the
paper quotes. That value comes from a different study (Ramirez 2019) and was
used in the paper only to justify assuming no drug effect after day 4 (Table S1,
assumption iv); it is not a parameter of the model. The PK layer reproduces the
Campagne 2019 parameters exactly, as the clearance check below shows, so the
difference is between the two source studies, not an error in the translation.

The dose-normalised AUC is the same for both doses, as the linear PK layer
requires, and equals the dose divided by CL (Table S2).

```{r pknca-linearity}
auc_norm <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  mutate(dose_umol = ifelse(treatment == "100 mg/kg", 100, 25) / mw_cy,
         cl_est = dose_umol / PPORRES)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_norm$cl_est / 4.4 - 1) < 0.02))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dosing input.** The paper (Eq. 1) describes a 9-min zero-order input, but
  the parameters were calibrated with the authors' code, whose time stepping
  delivered 4 times the nominal dose over the 0.025-day step before each nominal
  dose time (see "Dosing input"). The packaged model keeps the paper's equations
  and values; the published figures are reproduced here with the as-fitted
  input, and the nominal input is shown for contrast. The model itself does not
  encode either input: the event table does.
* **PK-to-T-cell coupling.** The authors' code solved the PK first and drove
  the T-cell model with the 4HCY concentration held constant over each
  0.025-day step at its end-of-step value. The packaged model couples the layers
  continuously, as the paper's equations do. This changes the day-7 values after
  25-100 mg/kg by 0.6- to 2.7-fold, changes day 21 by at most about 6%, and has
  no effect in the vehicle arm or by day 200.
* **Values from the authors' code.** Table 1 rounds the estimated parameters to
  three significant figures; the model carries the full-precision values from
  the authors' notebook (m21, m31, m41, hreg, lambda0, capacities). The initial
  donor T cells in blood (34.3% of the 40 x 10^6 infused splenocytes, CD4:CD8
  ratio 0.598, 0.4% Treg among CD4+ cells) and the exact molar mass of CY
  (0.261086 mg/umol) appear only in the notebook.
* **Blood volume needs body weight.** `WT` (kg) is a time-varying covariate
  used only for the blood concentration outputs. The vignette supplies each
  cohort's fitted weight spline (Methods S2, Data S2). Tissue outputs do not
  depend on it.
* **Time origin.** The thymic-output function uses the time since transplant,
  so simulations must start at day 0 = donor-graft infusion.
* **One residual error, twelve parameters.** The paper estimated a single
  proportional error xi = 0.821 for all T-cell outputs. rxode2 needs a separate
  error parameter per endpoint, so each of the twelve outputs carries
  `propSd_<output> = 0.821`; re-estimating the model would treat them as
  independent unless they are tied.
* **Neural-network GVHD layer not included.** The GVHD score was predicted by a
  three-layer scikit-learn MLP (final model: 15 hidden ReLU nodes, inputs dose,
  body weight, time, previous observed score, blood and liver Treg). Its weights
  and biases were not published, so it cannot be reproduced.
* **Fixed versus estimated.** Parameters taken from the literature, calibrated
  by hand or set from the maximum observation are wrapped in `fixed()`; the
  eight estimated by Nelder-Mead (m21, m31, m41, hreg, lambda_b, lambda0,c,
  lambda0,reg, xi) are not. There is no between-animal variability.
* **CY half-life.** The PKNCA half-life is compared with the 0.19 h value the
  paper quotes from a different study (Ramirez 2019); the PK layer itself is the
  Campagne 2019 model, so an exact match is not expected.
